pages.name: Resolution Mechanic
pages.html:
Resolution Mechanic: Spacer uses two six-sided dice, abbreviated to 2D, to resolve actions. Any actions that require a check is determined by the following:

2D + Relevant DMs + Relevant Skill Rank:
Results of 8+ are a success.

Using DMs: Characteristic DMs are always applied, but the referee may also include DMs from situation factors and environmental factors as well.

Effect of a Roll: The difference between the rolled total and the amount needed to succeed on a roll.

  • For example, if a player rolled 6 and needed 8+, then they have an effect of -2. If the same character rolled 10, then they have an effect of +2.

Book p.14

pages.name: When to Roll?
pages.html:
When to Roll?: Rolls are only necessary when under stress or in a conflict, where failure results in consequences for failing, such as:

  • Impacting Narrative Consequences: Being denied permission, failing to persuade a random NPC to not attack them, losing a business deal, etc.
  • Loss of Resources: Time, ammo, repair parts, fuel, etc., may be wasted on a failure result.
  • Harm or Death: When wounded, poisoned, exposed to environmental hazards that require survival actions.
  • Complications: If failure would be interesting to the story, such as being caught trespassing, failing to bypass a robot’s warranty, failing to jury-rig a ship’s damaged maneuver drive, etc.

Roleplaying over Rolling: Players and referees are expected to prioritize roleplaying and communicating their actions. Gameplay happens between dice rolls. Rolling dice is only used to determine the results of roleplaying; they are not the driving force of roleplaying. This means that rolls are not made to resolve all actions. If the characters have no urgency or external factors that could impact their ability to perform a task, then a roll is not necessary.

Book p.14

pages.name: Who Rolls?
pages.html:
The player rolls for:

  • Character Actions: When the character declares intention to take an action they are in control of, they will roll for themselves as needed. Remember: this is only needed when failure has a consequence.

The referee rolls for:

  • Unknown Information: Any actions or circumstances that the characters would not have knowledge or awareness of, such as NPC motivations, social links between power groups, or general knowledge that the spears may not have immediate access to.
  • Interactions with NPCs: When characters interact with NPCs, the referee determines any NPC-associated motives or qualities, such as reactions and morale, using the associated tables if necessary.

Book p.14

pages.name: Absolute Successes and Failures
pages.html:
Optional - Absolute Successes and Failures: When rolling 2D, there is a small chance of a task or situation becoming more beneficial or complicated due to how the dice land.

  • Absolute Success: When a character or referee rolls two sixes (boxcars), then the referee makes a ruling about what additional benefit occurs in gameplay. Examples could be a task takes 1/2 as long to do, the character earns the trust of an NPC, a tip is added to the payment they negotiated, etc. In combat, this allows a weapon to deal full damage.
  • Absolute Failure: When a character or referee rolls two ones (snake eyes), then the referee makes a ruling about what additional drawback occurs in addition to failure. This could be more time or resources wasted, an NPC thinks the character is a liar, etc. In combat, this causes a weapon to misfire and become jammed or the melee weapon becomes too damaged to use.

Chances of Absolute Results: There is a 2.78% chance of rolling either an absolute success or failure each, so in total there is a 5.56% chance of getting those face die results. The referee should consider these odds before deciding to include or exclude using absolute results in their game.

Remember: Many situations may call for different types of checks, and how those situations are approached is open to interpretation and elaboration, based on the character. There is no set characteristic and Skill combination for use; it's all narrative dependent. However, It is ultimately up to the referee to decide which Skills and DMs from which characteristics may be applied, based on the circumstances of the current narrative.

Book p.14
